description: A single-track audio looper with its own clock, metronome click and pre-roll, recording loops a set number of bars long

params.text: Resets the beat counter, so the next clock counts as a bar clock
Sets the tempo of the internal clock, 30.0 to 300.0 BPM; changing it does not stretch loops already recorded
Sets the time signature, from 2/4 up to 15/8, which sets how many clocks make a bar
Sends the metronome click to the CLICK output
Sets the level of the click, 0 to 200%
Counts a bar or two of click in before the track starts, but only when the track is stopped
Chooses whether the pre-roll counts one bar or two
Starts the track, or stops it if it is already playing, recording or overdubbing; with a cable in the ALL STOP jack this only starts
Sets the level of the stereo input, 0 to 200%, with the centre at 100%
Silences the input; it has to be off before anything can be recorded
Sets how many bars the loop lasts, 1 to 16
Ties the track to the clock, so a command takes effect on the next bar; with it off the track starts and stops at once and the MEAS knob is ignored for recording
Starts an idle track at the position the bar has already reached, instead of waiting for the loop to come round
Stops a playing or overdubbing track at once with an 8ms fade, instead of waiting for the loop to end
Plays, records or overdubs the loop once and then leaves the track idle
Plays or overdubs the loop backwards; the direction changes only when the loop reaches its end
Sets the crossfade between the end of a loop and its restart, 0 to 1000ms, and the fades the manual describes elsewhere; it comes up at 8ms
Pans the track's own stereo output; the main outputs and what is recorded are not panned
Sets the level of the track's output, 0% to 100%
Starts recording on an empty track, or overdubbing on one that already holds a loop
Starts playback of the recorded loop; the PLAY Button Sequence menu item changes what repeated presses do
Stops playback, recording or overdubbing
Double-click to erase the recorded loop; it only works while the track is idle
Sends the source signal straight to the track's own outputs as well

inputs.text: The left channel of the source to record; with nothing in the right jack this one is used for both
The right channel of the source to record
A trigger here does what the REC button does
A trigger here does what the PLAY button does
A trigger here does what the STOP button does
A trigger here erases the recorded loop
Plays the loop faster or slower, one octave per volt, which changes its pitch
A trigger here flips the loop's playback direction, as the REV button does
Moves the pan, over the range chosen under PAN CV range
An external clock to follow instead of the internal one; with a cable here the clock is treated as always running
A trigger here resets the beat counter and restarts the synced loop
A trigger here does what the STRT/STOP button does
A trigger here stops the track, and leaves the STRT/STOP jack free to start it

outputs.text: The left channel of the track output
The right channel of the track output
A 1ms pulse when the loop reaches its end, and on a forced stop when 'EOL pulse on stop' is ticked
A 1ms pulse on every clock, generated or received
A pulse when the beat counter is reset

notes: nothing is recorded until the MUTE button is off and a source is connected; the level is set with the LVL knob while you test it.
a loop is recorded for an extra second past its end, the recording tail, and the XFD crossfade is taken from that tail.
an imported loop has no recording tail, which is what the 'Extra samples Tail (1sec)' setting on the track menu is for.
the PLAY and REC lights show the state: both off is empty, PLAY lit steady is idle, PLAY flashing is playing, REC flashing is recording, both flashing is overdubbing.
a fast flash on PLAY or REC means a command has been given and takes effect at the end of the loop; pressing the same button again cancels it.
the vertical bar shows the position in the loop and its colour shows the state: black empty, red first recording, blue idle, green playing, yellow overdubbing.
right-clicking the track's bar display opens the track menu: Fade IN on playback, Play Full Tail on Stop, Import Wav, Export Wav, Extra samples Tail (1sec), Detect tempo and set bpm.
with a synced loop and a V/Oct voltage away from 0V the loop cannot be played exactly to the bar.
above C4 a synced loop finishes early and there is silence before it restarts; below C4 it is cut off when the bar comes round.
menu: PLAY Button Sequence — sets what the PLAY button and its jack do: start and stop, or record then play then overdub, or record then overdub then play, with STOP the only way out of the last two
Instant STOP button — makes the STOP button drop the track to idle at once, except during the first recording of a synced track
OVERDUB after REC — moves the track into overdub by itself at the end of its first recording
EOL pulse on stop — sends a pulse from the EoL output when the loop is forced to stop as well as at its natural end
PAN CV range: 0/10v, ± 5v, ±10v — sets the voltage span the PAN CV jack covers
Track settings — opens the same items the track's bar display carries, from the module's own menu
Internal Clock Always ON — keeps the internal clock running even with the track idle, as an external clock does
Click Settings — a submenu choosing between the three built-in click pairs, or loading a wav file for the beat click and another for the bar click
Add Expander — places a sickoLooperX to the right, adding another track under this module's clock
